title: Gallai's two-per-class colouring theorem
statement: Let $G$ be a finite simple graph whose chromatic number equals $k$. Suppose $G$ admits a proper colouring, using some number $n$ of colours, in which every one of the $n$ colour classes contains at least two vertices. Then $G$ admits a proper colouring with exactly $k$ colours in which, likewise, every colour class contains at least two vertices.
hypotheses_covered: there exists a proper colouring with $n$ colours in which every colour class has at least two vertices
replaced:
\emph{ (B\&M \S{}8.1, verbatim; T. Gallai).  }If a \texttt{k}-chromatic graph
\texttt{G} has a colouring in which each colour is assigned to at least two vertices,
show that \texttt{G} has a \texttt{k}-colouring of this type.*
